title: BENDING-PATCH: constant-curvature patch test of the Q4 Mindlin plate element

gates.reference: constant-curvature field, closed form; Zienkiewicz & Taylor Vol.2
constant-curvature closed form (patch test, exact reproduction)
1/2 kappa^T Db kappa * Area (documented: MITC shear sampling on a skew element is not exactly shear-free)

gates.quantity: worst |w_free/w_symmetry - 1/(1-nu^2)| / (1/(1-nu^2)) over the strip mesh set, w taken from the two computed solutions
gates.reference: ratio of the two rigidities, D/D_b = 1/(1-nu^2)

gates.quantity: observed order of the distorted patch, w (round-off-limited treatments excluded; n/a -> fail)
min tip-deflection error of the locking element (thin strip, t/L = 0.01)
gates.reference: shear locking must be visible (negative control)

gates.quantity: max energy error of the locking element on the patch
gates.reference: shear locking must be visible (negative control)

gates.quantity: max |K_ff u_f + K_fc u_c| over all patch cases

limitations: A patch test is a consistency (necessary) condition; it proves constant-curvature reproduction, not coarse-mesh accuracy or pointwise moment accuracy.

On non-affine (distorted) patches the sri element leaves a bilinear-w interpolation residual against the quadratic exact field; it is measured, h-convergent and inside the case-pool tolerance, not a consistency defect. The mitc element reproduces the same state to round-off, so an observed order is not defined for it and the order gate excludes round-off-limited treatments.

The observed-order gate is defined only above a declared round-off floor (1e-10 relative); a treatment whose error is at machine precision is reported as 'order not defined' and excluded rather than fitted.
A Dirichlet-driven patch contains no zero-energy mode, so this test cannot detect the rank deficiency of the one-point (sri) element.

Literature criterion cited from the standard statement; the textbooks were not retrievable offline, but every target value is evaluated in code from the closed form, so no table digit enters the evidence chain.

The Poisson cross-check grades the ratio of the two *computed* tip deflections. The ratio of the two closed-form rigidities is an algebraic identity (1/(1-nu^2) for any element) and is reported only as a reference value, never as accuracy evidence.

The free-edge strip is compared with the 1-D beam closed form, which is not the exact solution of a width/thickness = 20 Mindlin plate: the residual converges to a plateau under through-width refinement (~1.3% for sri, ~1.3% for mitc) instead of vanishing. The gate therefore compares models, not just meshes, and its margin is the thinnest of the anchor.
